tra_loi.Q1: The British. A Union Jack flies on the tower on the Rock (frames 40-41), and the Rock's fort has Union Jack-style flags in the later frames. This is a guess from the flag alone, because no text names them.
tra_loi.Q2: "1779 — The Great Siege" (frame 23). It starts with a ring of tents and a line of troops and cattle on the plain beside the Rock, which looks like a land blockade or camp. It then continues with ships gathering in the bay.
tra_loi.Q3: Not sure. The pictures suggest the town is cut off by a blockade: a siege camp on land and ships around the bay. No picture shows hunger, empty food stores or starving people. Frames 41-42 show people lying or tumbling on a hillside, which might mean exhaustion, but this isn't clear.
tra_loi.Q4: Ships. Sailing ships arrive in the bay (frames 36-38 and 47), and a convoy of many ships sits off the town in frames 53-56. I can't tell from the pictures alone whether they are a relief fleet or enemy ships. A line of people carries barrels or supplies into the fort in frames 48-49, which hints at resupply.

tra_loi.Q1: The British hold it. A Union Jack flies from the tower on the Rock in frames 40-41 (Jan 1780). The Rock is not shown with any other flag.
tra_loi.Q2: '1779 — The Great Siege' (frame 23, 21 Jun 1779). Rows of tents and a long line of troops and animals build up on the plain facing the Rock, and ships gather in the bay, so it is a siege of the town by an army and fleet.
tra_loi.Q3: The pictures do not show hunger directly. They suggest the town is cut off. A besieging camp blocks it on land, and ships sit offshore. A few ships come and go in the bay, but the pictures show no food, no starving people and no rations, so my answer is partly inference. Not sure.
tra_loi.Q4: Ships. A single ship and later a small group of ships sail across the bay toward the town (frames 36-38, 47 and 52). The pictures do not show what they carry or that they relieve the town. Not sure what the ships bring.

tra_loi.Q1: The British. A Union Jack flies over the fortress tower on the Rock in frames 40-41 (Jan 1780), and the town is shown under siege from the land side and the sea throughout.
